## Purpose and runtime
Yuvomi is a self-hosted household-management application: modular tasks, calendar, finance, kitchen, documents, health, family, and automation features for up to six users. It runs as a Node.js 22+ Express service with a vanilla ES-module/PWA client, backed by one SQLite database with optional SQLCipher encryption. Container deployment is primary: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `entrypoint.sh`.

## Application entry points
The server starts in `server/index.js`, initializes persistence through `server/db.js`, and serves both API routes and static client assets. Authentication/session behavior is centered in `server/auth.js`; authorization and scoped access are in `server/permissions.js` and `server/scopes.js`. Browser startup begins at `public/index.html`, with routing in `public/router.js` and API access in `public/api.js`.

## Client shell and module UI
The frontend is framework-free and composed from page modules, reusable components, settings pages, and shared utilities. Route-selected pages call the server API and render household-domain screens; settings manage module activation, personal preferences, integrations, and administration.
Key paths: `public/pages/dashboard.js`, `public/pages/calendar.js`, `public/pages/tasks.js`; `public/settings/registry.js`, `public/components/detail-view.js`.

## HTTP API and domain boundary
Express routes provide the operational API, organized mostly by household domain. Route handlers enforce validation, CSRF protections, idempotency where applicable, authentication, permissions, and visibility before invoking domain services and database operations. The OpenAPI definition mirrors the public HTTP contract and supports API-token consumers.
Key paths: `server/routes/tasks.js`, `server/routes/calendar.js`, `server/routes/documents.js`; `server/middleware/csrf.js`, `server/middleware/idempotency.js`; `server/openapi.js`.

## Persistence, tenancy, and security
`server/db.js` owns schema setup/migrations and SQLite/SQLCipher access. Household membership, roles, module capabilities, per-entity visibility, and API token scopes form the primary data-access boundary. The system supports password authentication, invite onboarding, TOTP, optional OIDC, password reset, and admin-only operations.
Key paths: `server/db.js`, `server/auth.js`, `server/services/visibility.js`; `server/services/oidc.js`, `server/services/two-factor.js`.

## Cross-module workflows and scheduling
Services implement business workflows beyond CRUD: meal-to-shopping export, pantry expiry alerts, task rewards, shared-expense calculations, document linking, generated calendar overlays, and recurring/reminder processing. Background/scheduled behaviors are hosted in-process rather than as a separate worker.
Key paths: `server/services/meal-recurrence.js`, `server/services/pantry-reminders.js`, `server/services/event-reminder-fanout.js`; `server/services/backup-scheduler.js`, `server/services/push-scheduler.js`.

## External integrations and operational boundaries
External calls are opt-in and guarded against SSRF/private-network targets by default. Integrations include Google Calendar/Drive, CalDAV/CardDAV, Microsoft Graph Outlook push, WebDAV backup/document storage, Mealie/Tandoor recipe mirrors, OIDC, email, Gotify, ntfy, generic webhooks, Immich, and GitHub release checks. Backup/restore is an explicit subsystem with optional WebDAV upload.
Key paths: `server/services/caldav-sync.js`, `server/services/google-calendar.js`, `server/services/document-storage.js`; `server/services/notification-providers/guarded-fetch.js`, `server/routes/backup.js`.

## Extension and agent interfaces
Module activation/capability logic permits independently enabled built-in and drop-in modules. API tokens expose the OpenAPI-described API; an MCP server provides AI-agent tooling while applying router permissions. The PWA service worker supplies offline/static caching and installation behavior.
Key paths: `server/services/modules.js`, `server/services/module-capabilities.js`; `server/mcp/server.js`, `server/mcp/tools.js`; `public/sw.js`, `public/manifest.json`.
